summary: 东印度公司的茶叶贸易垄断结束后，最先把当季新茶送到英国便可能获得溢价。美国率先发展飞剪船，英美海员的竞争继而演变成从中国茶港到伦敦码头的竞速。
logic: 垄断贸易偏爱载重慢船
新茶溢价提高航速的价值
美国造快船、英国改进船型
茶港抢先装船并赶潮抵达伦敦

paragraphs.brief: 17世纪和18世纪，英国东印度公司垄断了与中国和印度的贸易。
sentences: During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the British East India Company had the monopoly on trade with China and India.
17世纪和18世纪，英国东印度公司垄断了与中国和印度的贸易。
This meant that because no rival could legally import tea or other goods from these countries at this time, the company was rarely in a hurry to transport its merchandise.
这意味着，由于目前没有任何竞争对手能够合法地从这些国家进口茶叶或其他货物，该公司很少急于运输其商品。
Instead, its priority was to minimise costs by carrying as much as possible on each ship.
相反，它的优先事项是通过尽可能多地载运每艘船舶来尽量减少费用。
This meant that its ships – known as East Indiamen – were enormous, strong and very slow.
这意味着其船只——称为东印度人——是巨大的、强大的和非常缓慢的。

paragraphs.brief: 他们将在那里收满当年的茶收成，再次起动，并视风和天气而定，打算在下一年9月之前运回，因此即使航行条件有利，往返旅行也持续了将近两年，如果出了差错，需要更长的时间。
sentences: By 1800, the average East Indiaman could carry 1,200 tons of merchandise.
到1800年，平均的东印度人可以携带1200吨商品。

The trading pattern for China tea usually meant the East Indiamen set sail from Britain in January, sailed round the Cape of Good Hope at the southernmost tip of Africa, and arrived in China in September.
中国茶的贸易模式通常意味着印度东部人于1月从英国出发，在非洲最南端的好望角航行，并于9月抵达中国。

There they would load up that year’s tea harvest, set off again and, depending on the wind and weather, aim to arrive back by the following September, so even with favourable sailing conditions, the round trip lasted almost two years, and if anything went wrong it could take a lot longer.
他们将在那里收满当年的茶收成，再次起动，并视风和天气而定，打算在下一年9月之前运回，因此即使航行条件有利，往返旅行也持续了将近两年，如果出了差错，需要更长的时间。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，到1834年，该公司失去了其贸易垄断，茶叶已成为自由交易的物品。
sentences: However, by 1834 the company had lost its trading monopolies, and tea had become a freely traded item.
然而，到1834年，该公司失去了其贸易垄断，茶叶已成为自由交易的物品。
Having no more use for its great ships, the company sold them off, and many were bought by merchants or their captains, who continued to plough the seas between Britain and China.
该公司不再使用其大船，因此将其出售，许多是商人或船长购买的，他们继续在英国和中国之间的海上进行耕作。
But now that tea could be traded freely, a few smart sailors began to realise that whoever brought each new harvest of tea to Britain first stood to make the most money.
但是现在茶可以自由交易，几个聪明的水手开始意识到，谁把每块茶新的收获给英国首先是赚最多的钱。

paragraphs.brief: 茶贩现在需要更快的闲置船只才能把贵重货物带回来
sentences: This was partly because if you were home first, you could sell your shipment of tea before your competitors even arrived, and partly because consumers in Britain in the nineteenth century believed that the fresher and earlier-picked the tea, the better the resulting drink.
这部分是因为如果你先回家，你可以在竞争对手到来之前卖掉你的茶，部分是因为十九世纪英国消费者认为更新鲜更早地挑茶，最终的饮料越好。
Tea traders now needed faster, sleeker ships to bring their precious cargo back.
茶贩现在需要更快的闲置船只才能把贵重货物带回来

Nevertheless, in Britain this idea only caught on slowly, and while the 1840s saw a few faster ships launched, for the time being many merchants remained satisfied with the slow but reliable East Indiamen.
然而，在英国，这一想法只是缓慢地被抓住，1840年代时，发射了几艘更快的船舶，目前许多商人对缓慢但可靠的东印度人仍然感到满意。

paragraphs.brief: 1850年代和1860年代，英国设计并建造了更多的茶叶剪片；它们的光束比美国的相距窄，在风暴中较弱，但在较平静的天气中则较快。
sentences: In fact it was the Americans who pioneered the first clipper ships.
事实上，是美国人先发制人首艘剪刀船。
These vessels were fast and slender, with a narrow hull that was deeper at the back than at the front, and masses of sails on tall masts.
这些船是快速的和苗条的，后面的船体比前面更深，高上的帆船。
They earned their name from the way that they ‘clipped off’ journey time.
他们从他们 " 离开 " 的旅途中赢得了自己的名字。
British merchants resolved to build their own clippers to rival the Americans, and the first British tea clipper, Stornaway, was built in Aberdeen in 1850.
英国商人决心建立自己的剪刀来对抗美国人 1850年在阿伯丁建造了第一台英国茶剪刀

More tea clippers were designed and built in Britain throughout the 1850s and 1860s; they had a narrower beam than their American equivalents, making them less powerful during storms but faster in calmer weather.
1850年代和1860年代，英国设计并建造了更多的茶叶剪片；它们的光束比美国的相距窄，在风暴中较弱，但在较平静的天气中则较快。

paragraphs.brief: 英国和美国的船在茶叶交易中有着巨大的竞争精神但首先美国人有优势
sentences: There was a great spirit of competition between the British and American ships plying the tea trade, but to begin with the Americans had the edge.
英国和美国的船在茶叶交易中有着巨大的竞争精神但首先美国人有优势
Then in 1851 a British shipowner, Richard Green, built the aptly named clipper Challenger with the stated intention of beating the American ships.
1851年英国船主理查德·格林建造了这个叫得上"挑战者"的剪刀目的是要打败美国船只
Loaded with tea, Challenger left China for London in 1852 at the same time as the American clipper Challenge, a much larger, older ship already greatly admired for its speed.
1852年挑战者号带着茶离开中国前往伦敦与美国的剪报机挑战号同时一艘更庞大更老的飞船已经因其速度而备受敬佩
Large sums were bet on which would complete the journey first.
押注了大笔资金，将首先完成旅程。
In the event, the British ship beat its rival to London by two days, amid much jubilation.
英国舰艇在欢庆中击败了前往伦敦的对手两天。
From then on, such international races grew in popularity.
从那时起，这种国际赛事越来越受欢迎。

paragraphs.brief: 1855年后，美国逐渐停止参与英国茶叶贸易。
sentences: After 1855, American participation in the British tea trade gradually stopped.
1855年后，美国逐渐停止参与英国茶叶贸易。
But even without the Anglo-American rivalry, the competitive spirit continued.
但是，即使没有英美竞争，竞争精神仍在继续。
It was really ignited when new ports were opened up for trade in China.
中国开放新港口供贸易时，它真正被点燃了。
These included Foochow, which was much closer to the tea-producing areas than Canton, the port used previously.
其中包括Foochow，它比以前使用的港口Canton更接近茶叶生产区。

As a result, tea could be loaded on board earlier and fresher, and the clippers could set off in late May or early June – sometimes not even taking time to fill out the official paperwork – racing back to Britain whatever the difficulties.
因此，茶可以更早、更新鲜地装上，剪报机可以在5月底或6月初开始 — — 有时甚至没有花时间填写正式文件 — — 无论遇到什么困难，都回到了英国。

paragraphs.brief: 穿过亚速尔河穿过英吉利海峡进入泰晤士河河口
sentences: They sped down through the South China Sea and into the Indian Ocean, then raced to get round the southernmost tip of Africa at the Cape of Good Hope.
他们冲过南中国海冲进印度洋然后跑到好望角的非洲最南端
Then it was north across the vast Atlantic, past the Azores, through the English Channel and into the estuary of the River Thames.
穿过亚速尔河穿过英吉利海峡进入泰晤士河河口
Once there, they would be towed by tugs up the river and into the docks.
一旦到了那里，他们就会被拖上河，拖进码头。

paragraphs.brief: 胜船的货物每磅可得到高达6便士的溢价，因此船长和船员得到货主的奖励。
sentences: The cargo of the winning ship could earn a premium of up to sixpence per pound – and so the captain and crew were rewarded by the owners of the cargo.
胜船的货物每磅可得到高达6便士的溢价，因此船长和船员得到货主的奖励。
But the races were about more than just money: the crews, about 40 men on each clipper, were expert sailors, proud of their ships, and they delighted in competing against each other.
但比赛不仅仅是钱：每支剪刀上大约有40人，他们是专家水手，为他们的船感到骄傲，他们很高兴能够相互竞争。

Without their enthusiasm, the races would never have happened, since getting home as fast as possible required the crew to be totally dedicated and to sacrifice much of their rest for the duration of the race.
没有他们的热情，比赛就永远不会发生，因为尽快回家需要全体船员全心全意地奉献，在比赛期间牺牲他们的大部分休息时间。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the British East India Company faced a lot of competition.
items.zh: 17世纪和18世纪，英国东印度公司面临许多竞争。
items.why: 当时东印度公司垄断对华、对印贸易，与“面临激烈竞争”相矛盾。

items.en: Before 1800, cargo size was the most important consideration for the East India Company.
items.zh: 1800年以前，货物规模是东印度公司最重要的考虑因素。
items.why: 段落 1 末句提到公司“prioritisea minimising costs by carrying as much as possible on each ship"一一货物量 (船舱容量) 是最重要的考量。

items.en: At best, voyages of the East Indiamen to China and back took nearly two years to complete.
items.zh: 东印度人回中国的旅程最多花了将近两年时间才完成
items.why: 即使航行条件有利，往返也要到次年九月左右才能完成，合计接近两年。

items.en: Before 1834, voyages to and from China were considered to be highly dangerous.
items.zh: 1834年以前，往返中国的航程被认为是高度危险的。
items.why: 文中写风向和天气影响往返所需时间，没有说1834年前人们认为这段航程极其危险。

items.en: After 1834, the ships which had served the East India Company stopped being used for commercial purposes.
items.zh: 1834年以后，为东印度公司服务的船舶不再用于商业目的。
items.why: 公司出售旧船后，商人和船长继续用它们航行贸易，商业用途并未终止。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, British drinkers preferred tea made from mature leaves to that made from younger leaves.
items.zh: 在十九世纪，英国的饮酒者更喜欢用成熟的叶子制成的茶，而不是用较年轻的叶子制出的茶。
items.why: 段落 4 指出英国消费者相信“the fresher and earlier-picked the tea, the bette斑，偏好嫩叶而非“成熟叶”。

items.en: The ships were remarkable for the number of ________ they had.
items.zh: 这些帆船以________数量众多而著称。
items.why: 回到对应内容“这些船是快速的和苗条的，后面的船体比前面更深，高上的帆船”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The performance of British tea clippers was particularly affected when there were ________ at sea.
items.zh: 海上出现________时，英国运茶快帆船的航行表现尤其容易受影响。
items.why: 回到对应内容“1850年代和1860年代，英国设计并建造了更多的茶叶剪片；它们的光束比美国的相距窄，在风暴中较弱，但在较平静的天气中则较快”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: It was in a ship called ________ that the British first competed successfully against the Americans.
items.zh: 英国人第一次成功与美国人竞争，靠的是一艘名为________的船。
items.why: 段落 6:“the aptly named clipper Challenger…beat its rivaP一第一次成功挑战美国船只即在 Challenger 号上完成。

items.en: Competition increased when additional Chinese trading ________ were established.
items.zh: 随着中国增设通商________，竞争愈发激烈。
items.why: 回到对应内容“中国开放新港口供贸易时，它真正被点燃了”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Merchants were occasionally in such a hurry that they failed to complete the ________ before leaving China.
items.zh: 商人有时急于启航，离开中国前甚至没办完________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“因此，茶可以更早、更新鲜地装上，剪报机可以在5月底或6月初开始 — — 有时甚至没有花时间填写正式文件 — — 无论遇到什么困难，都回到了英国”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: At the end of their journey, the ships needed the help of ________.
items.zh: 航程即将结束时，这些帆船需要________的协助。
items.why: 回到对应内容“一旦到了那里，他们就会被拖上河，拖进码头”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The crews were motivated by both ________ and their enthusiasm for the competition.
items.zh: 船员们的动力既来自________，也来自他们对竞赛的热情。
items.why: 回到对应内容“但比赛不仅仅是钱：每支剪刀上大约有40人，他们是专家水手，为他们的船感到骄傲，他们很高兴能够相互竞争”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 第 9 段 · 第 2 句
第 7 段 · 第 4 句
points: 文中写风向和天气影响往返所需时间，没有说1834年前人们认为这段航程极其危险。
回到对应内容“这些船是快速的和苗条的，后面的船体比前面更深，高上的帆船”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: This meant that …, the company was rarely in a hurry to transport its merchandise.
连接词 because 引出“because no rival could legally import tea or other goods from these countries at this time”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
…, a few smart sailors began to realise that whoever brought each new harvest of tea to Britain first stood to make the most money.
“But now that tea could be traded freely”补足 began 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 began 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
